title.narrative: Youth Inclusion in Jordan's Development Process

description.narrative:
There is a growing recognition of the value of the Education for the sustainable development for all learners and for the unique role of the univeristies plau in the transformation of indviduals, institutions and societies towards more sustainable futures. Universities engage and lead in several areas: education, research and community engagemet, all of which are essential in this transformation. further, given their focus and influence, universities are pivotal to action needed to realize the UN sustainable development goals.

Balqa Applied University (BAU) and their co-applicant Namaa beliwbw that they have a criticak role in both pursuuing and integrating the SDGs in their actions. SDGs combine an inspirational vision for transforming their world, whilst setting out an agenda for 2030. they believe SDGs when considered as an indivisble whole, are useful for education for sustainable development (ESD) in representing the wide framing and scope of sustainable development, illustrating a holistic view of interconnnected environmental, economnic, cultural and social issues and dimensions as well as encouraging interdisciplinarity. By including SDGs in teaching and learning, universities are enabling future graduates to contribute to global sustainability agenda; encouraging students to critically and constructively assess how SDGs can help empower them to effectively design the next steps towars the future.

throughthis project, BAU and Namaa will empower their targeted groups to make informed decisions and ressponsible actions for environmental integrity, economic visibility and a just society for present and future generations while respecting cultural diversity through social innovation, using new approaches and tools. They will contribute to a sustainable future and to achieving humanity's transformative challenge; which is providing a decent life and well-being of communities within their own resources and capacities with the hands of their young men and women.

the project will target 300 of its students in 3 governorates; 140 from Balqa, 60 from Madaba, and 100 from Aqqaba. 50% of targeted students are females and 5% are students with disabilities. Also, the project targets 15 BAU doctors to act as mentors to targeting sttudents, helping themm in their knowledge, skills, and attitude to be able to establish sustainable social businesses.

the project has 3 overall objectives:

1- contribute to SDG 11 "sustaiable cities and communities"

2- Foster young people's role in the development of their local communities

3- increase young skilled/ educated youth partcicipatoion in the labour market by encouraging them to start their own social intiatives and sustain it into a social business project.
